newsitem.title: USA: S&P's Grossman withdraws from N.J. rating team.
newsitem.headline: S&P's Grossman withdraws from N.J. rating team.

text.p: Hyman Grossman, one of Standard & Poor's Corp's best known credit analysts, has stepped down from the rating agency's New Jersey team after criticism of his ties to state politics, an S&P official told Reuters.

"Hy is one of the most respected municipal analysts in the business and it shows how much he cares about the process that he voluntarily stepped aside so that no one could even make the allegation that was made," Glenn Goldberg, a managing director at S&P, said in an interview.

Grossman came under fire last month from Republican lawmakers in the state, who said his criticism of Gov. Christine Whitman's $2.8 billion pension bond proposal stemmed from his ties to Democratic politics in the state.
Grossman is a member of the Marlboro Township Democratic Committee and has been active in Democratic causes for many years.
Grossman blasted the reports, pointing out that he had also been one of S&P's lead analysts when the agency downgraded New Jersey under former Democratic Gov. Jim Florio.
Goldberg said Grossman made the decision to recuse himself from the New Jersey team the day after the news reports surfaced in late May.
S&P is a unit of McGraw-Hill Cos Inc.
